steps.text: Drums are played by triggers: short pulses that say 'hit now'. A Euclidean sequencer spreads a number of hits as evenly as it can over a number of steps, which is how many rhythms of the world are built.
Patch X4 of the clock to CLOCK of the Euclidean sequencer. It now steps on every sixteenth note.
Patch GATE 1 of the Euclidean sequencer to KICK TRIG of the drums.
Patch MIX of the drums to jack 1 of the patchbay. Four kicks in sixteen steps: four on the floor.
Press Tab and turn HITS of track 1. Three hits in sixteen steps is a classic off-kilter groove; go back to four for the steady beat.
Press Tab and patch GATE 2 to SNARE TRIG and GATE 3 to HAT TRIG of the drums.
Press Tab and turn ROTATE of track 2. Rotate shifts the whole pattern later in time without changing it: find the spot where the snare sits on the backbeat.

A logic module combines gates: AND is high only while both inputs are. Press Tab, patch GATE 1 to A and GATE 3 to B of the logic module, and AND to CLAP TRIG of the drums: a clap only where kick and hat meet.
Press Tab and shape the kit: turn KICK DECAY for a short thump or a long boom, and SNARE TONE from drum body to snare wires.
Turn SWING of the clock up a little. Every second sixteenth now comes a bit late and the groove starts to shuffle.
A clock, a Euclidean sequencer, a bit of logic and a drum module make a whole beat. Try other numbers of steps and hits on tracks 3 and 4. Press Next to finish.
